newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedes prefer opposition's Bildt as PM vs Persson.
newsitem.headline: Swedes prefer opposition's Bildt as PM vs Persson.

text.p: More than half of the Swedish population would prefer Carl Bildt, leader of the opposition Moderate party, to be prime minister rather than current premier Goran Persson, a survey showed on Monday.
The poll by the Swedish Institute of Public Opinion and Research (SIFO) found only 25 percent of 1,000 repondents would choose Persson as prime minister if there was a vote between the two men.
Persson heads Sweden's minority Social Democratic government and has been prime minister since March 1996.
But 51 percent of the interviewees said they would prefer to have Bildt as prime minister.
Bildt, who was prime minister between 1991-94, has spent the past few years working as an international peace coordinator in Bosnia.
He is due to return to Swedish politics this spring to prepare his party for the general election in September 1998.
Twenty-three percent were undecided or were negative to both men, said the poll that was published in daily newspaper Svenska Dagbladet.
Bildt's popularity has increased since December 1995 when, in a similar poll, 43 percent of respondents preferred Bildt as prime minister.
Persson's popularity has fallen from 37 percent in the last poll.
The Social Democrats support has dropped in the polls to 26.5 percent from 45 percent at the time of the last election in 1994.
Meanwhile the Moderates support has risen to 32 percent from 22.5 percent.
